long_biography.plain_text:
Model hot-air balloon kits filled a makeshift workshop on Mowbray’s family dairy farm. At eighteen, he left university and moved to China with his older brother Mat, using a NZ$20,000 parental loan to establish production. Sister Anna later joined, helping the siblings turn the small operation into ZURU.

As co-chief executive, Nick concentrated on scale, brand building and automated manufacturing. The group developed mass-market toy lines, then applied the same production and digital-marketing capabilities to nappies, haircare, pet food and other consumer categories. ZURU’s third division is pursuing software-led, factory-built housing; Mat leads much of that construction programme, while Nick remains co-chief executive across the wider group.

Forbes in 2019 described ZURU as owned by Nick, Mat and Anna, whereas its 2022 feature described ownership by Nick and Mat. Deloitte and ZURU continue to credit all three siblings as founders, but current individual equity percentages and any change in Anna's ownership are not public. The dossier says privately held and does not assign a personal stake.
